title: Eco-friendly Cu/NiO nanoparticle synthesis for anticancer activity
author: Cahyana, Saputri, et al.

steps.title: Prepare plant material
steps.instruction: Collect Annona muricata L. leaves, wash thoroughly, air‑dry, and finely grind them in a blender.

steps.title: Macerate leaves in methanol
steps.instruction: Macerate the ground leaves with methanol at a 1:10 (w/v) ratio, then filter to separate the methanol extract (basic extract filtrate) from the residue.

steps.title: Partition methanol extract
steps.instruction: Transfer the methanol extract to a separating funnel and partition with n‑hexane at a 1:1 (v/v) ratio, mixing until complete separation, then collect the two fractions: n‑hexane (non‑polar) and methanol (polar).

steps.title: Concentrate methanol fraction
steps.instruction: Concentrate the methanol fraction using a rotary vacuum evaporator set to 40–50 °C to obtain a dry residue, and dissolve this residue in water to produce the aqueous leaf extract.

steps.title: Perform phytochemical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the aqueous extract for secondary metabolites, confirming the presence of alkaloids, flavonoids, polyphenols, tannins, saponins, terpenoids, and steroids; this extract will be used for Cu/NiO nanoparticle synthesis.

steps.title: Prepare cell‑culture growth medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve either d‑MEM or RPMI powder in 1 L deionized water; add 3.7 g NaHCO₃ for d‑MEM or 2 g NaHCO₃ for RPMI, filter the solution through a 0.2 µm filter, then add fetal bovine serum (FBS) and antibiotics, and store the completed medium at 4 °C.
